package.description: A featherweight live-wallpaper engine for Windows.

en-US.description: A featherweight live-wallpaper engine for Windows.
en-US.longDescription:
FeatherWall puts any video or image on your Windows desktop and adds a configurable clock
widget over it. It runs as a single process built on raw Win32, Direct3D 11 and
DirectComposition, with no browser engine, no launcher and no account.

It supports both desktop topologies, the classic WorkerW layout and the Windows 11 24H2+
raised desktop, and pauses playback when a fullscreen app is in front, the session is locked,
the connection is remote, or battery saver is on. A still wallpaper costs about 151 MB and
0.03 percent CPU, measured on a 2560x1600 display at 150 percent scaling.

A built-in gallery offers curated public domain and CC0 wallpapers from NASA and Wikimedia
Commons, downloaded directly from the source with no API key and no tracking.
en-US.name: FeatherWall
en-US.releaseNotes:
Five widget styles, a Style page to choose between them, and a Start menu entry.

Widget styles
- Classic: the look FeatherWall has always had. Upgrading keeps it.
- Editorial: the date in small accent capitals above a light clock, with a short accent rule.
- Glass dock: everything in one capsule on the top or bottom edge.
- Orbit: a clock dial that fills as the hour passes, with the record and battery as small rings.
- Poster: a big stacked clock with outlined hours and accent minutes.

Choosing a style
- Tray: right-click the feather, then Widget style.
- Settings, Style page: live previews, accent colour (automatic from the wallpaper or picked), size, position and monitor.

Upgrading
- Your desktop looks the same until you pick a new style. One notification tells you the styles exist.
- New installs start on Orbit with the music and battery widget on.

Also new
- A Start menu entry, added on first start. Delete it and it stays deleted.
- One soft shadow under every new style's widgets keeps them readable on any wallpaper.
- Track names in Hindi, Thai, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and decorative Unicode letters now show as text.
- The record keeps its 15 fps timer: a compositor animation was measured and cost more GPU.
